airtable_webhook.name: Airtable Webhook
airtable_webhook.description: Trigger workflow from Airtable record changes like create, update, and delete events (requires Airtable credentials)

subBlocks.title: Credentials
subBlocks.description: This trigger requires airtable credentials to access your account.

subBlocks.title: Base ID
subBlocks.description: The ID of the Airtable Base this webhook will monitor.

subBlocks.title: Table ID
subBlocks.description: The ID of the table within the Base that the webhook will monitor.

subBlocks.title: Include Full Record Data
subBlocks.description: Enable to receive the complete record data in the payload, not just changes.

subBlocks.title: Setup Instructions
subBlocks.defaultValue:
1. Connect your Airtable account using the "Select Airtable credential" button above.
2. Ensure you have provided the correct Base ID and Table ID above.
3. You can find your Base ID and Table ID in the Airtable URL: https://airtable.com/[baseId]/[tableId]/.... See Finding Airtable IDs for details.
4. The webhook will trigger whenever records are created, updated, or deleted in the specified table.
5. Make sure your Airtable account has appropriate permissions for the specified base.

payloads.description: The payloads of the Airtable changes

timestamp.description: Timestamp of the change

latestPayload.description: The most recent payload from Airtable

timestamp.description: ISO 8601 timestamp of the change

actionMetadata.description: Metadata about who made the change

source.description: Source of the change (e.g., client, publicApi)

changedTablesById.description: Tables that were changed (keyed by table ID)

changedRecordsById.description: Changed records keyed by record ID

cellValuesByFieldId.description: Cell values keyed by field ID

airtableChanges.description: Consolidated record creations and updates. Deleted record IDs remain in raw payloads.

changeType.description: Type of consolidated change: created or updated

azure_devops_build_failed.name: Azure DevOps Build Failed
azure_devops_build_failed.description: Trigger workflow when an Azure DevOps build fails, is canceled, or partially succeeds

subBlocks.title: Setup Instructions
subBlocks.defaultValue:
1. Open your Azure DevOps project and go to Project settings → Service hooks.
2. Click + Create subscription, choose Web Hooks, then Next.
3. For Trigger on this type of event, select Build completed.
4. Under Filters, set Build result to Failed (optionally add Canceled / Partially succeeded).
5. Click Next, paste the Webhook URL above into the URL field.
6. Leave other fields as defaults. Click Test to verify, then Finish.

triggeredBy.description: Display name of the person who triggered the build

triggeredByEmail.description: Email/unique name of the person who triggered the build, or null if not set

buildUrl.description: API URL for the build resource

azure_devops_webhook.name: Azure DevOps Webhook (All Service Hook Events)
azure_devops_webhook.description: Trigger on whichever service hook event types you configure in Azure DevOps. Sim does not filter deliveries for this trigger.

subBlocks.title: Setup Instructions
subBlocks.defaultValue:
1. Open your Azure DevOps project and go to Project settings → Service hooks.

subBlocks.title: API Key
subBlocks.placeholder: Enter your Checkr secret API key

subBlocks.title: Setup Instructions
subBlocks.defaultValue:
1. Enter your Checkr production secret API key above (staging keys are not supported). Find it in the Checkr Dashboard under Account Settings > Developer Settings.
2. When you deploy the workflow, Sim registers a webhook in Checkr and runs this workflow on Adverse Action Canceled events. Checkr signs every delivery with your API key, and Sim rejects unsigned requests.
3. Checkr allows at most two webhooks per account, and each deployed Checkr trigger uses one. To react to several events with one webhook, use All Events and branch on the event type.
4. The webhook is deleted from Checkr when you remove this trigger and redeploy.

circleback_meeting_completed.name: Circleback Meeting Completed
circleback_meeting_completed.description: Trigger workflow when a meeting is processed and ready in Circleback

subBlocks.title: Signing Secret
subBlocks.description: Validates that webhook deliveries originate from Circleback using HMAC-SHA256.

subBlocks.title: Setup Instructions
subBlocks.defaultValue:
Note: You need access to Circleback automations to set up webhooks. See the Circleback webhook documentation for details.
1. In Circleback, click Automations in the sidebar.
2. Create a new automation or edit an existing one.
3. Add a Send webhook request step to your automation.
4. Paste the Webhook URL from above into the Endpoint field.
5. Optionally, copy the Signing Secret from Circleback and paste it above to verify webhook signatures.
6. Toggle what to include in the request (Meeting notes, Action items, Transcript). For this trigger: All meeting data.
7. Click "Done" and save the automation.

timestamp.description: Timestamp in seconds

insights.description: User-created insights keyed by insight name

confluence_attachment_created.name: Confluence Attachment Created
confluence_attachment_created.description: Trigger workflow when an attachment is uploaded in Confluence

subBlocks.title: Webhook Secret
subBlocks.description: Optional secret to validate webhook deliveries from Confluence using HMAC signature

subBlocks.title: Confluence Domain
subBlocks.description: Your Confluence Cloud domain

subBlocks.title: Confluence Email
subBlocks.description: Your Atlassian account email. Required together with API token to download attachment files.

subBlocks.title: API Token
subBlocks.description: API token from https://id.atlassian.com/manage-profile/security/api-tokens. Required to download attachment file content.

subBlocks.title: Include File Content
subBlocks.description: Download and include actual file content from attachments. Requires email, API token, and domain.

subBlocks.title: Setup Instructions
subBlocks.defaultValue:
Note: You must have admin permissions in your Confluence workspace to create webhooks. See the Confluence webhook documentation for details.
1. In Confluence, navigate to Settings > Webhooks.
2. Click "Create a Webhook" to add a new webhook.
3. Paste the Webhook URL from above into the URL field.
4. Optionally, enter the Webhook Secret from above into the secret field for added security.
5. Select the events you want to trigger this workflow. For this trigger, select attachment_created.
6. Click "Create" to activate the webhook.

timestamp.description: Timestamp of the webhook event (Unix epoch milliseconds)

userAccountId.description: Account ID of the user who triggered the event

spaceKey.description: Space key the content belongs to

lastModifierAccountId.description: Account ID of the last modifier

self.description: URL link to the content

files.description: Attachment file content downloaded from Confluence (if includeFileContent is enabled with credentials)

fivetran_connection_failure.name: Fivetran Connection Failed

subBlocks.title: Group ID
subBlocks.placeholder: Leave empty for every group in the account

subBlocks.title: Setup Instructions
subBlocks.defaultValue:
1. Enter a Fivetran API key and secret above. In Fivetran, click your username, then API Key > Generate API key. The key acts with your permissions, so it must be able to manage webhooks for the account or group.
2. Leave Group ID empty to receive events from every destination in the account, or enter a group ID to limit the webhook to that destination.
3. When you deploy the workflow, Sim registers a webhook in Fivetran for Connection Failed events with its own signing secret, and rejects deliveries that are not signed with it.
4. The webhook is deleted from Fivetran when you remove this trigger and redeploy.

generic_webhook.description: Receive webhooks from any service or API

subBlocks.title: Require Authentication
subBlocks.description: Require authentication for all webhook requests

subBlocks.title: Authentication Token
subBlocks.description: Token used to authenticate webhook requests via Bearer token or custom header

subBlocks.title: Secret Header Name (Optional)
subBlocks.description: Custom HTTP header name for the auth token. If blank, uses "Authorization: Bearer TOKEN"

subBlocks.title: Accept Other HTTP Methods
subBlocks.description: Also accept GET, PUT, PATCH and DELETE — no others — and expose the method under "method". Leave off unless you need it: a GET URL can be replayed by link prefetchers and scanners, and a request with no body cannot be deduplicated.

subBlocks.title: Expose Request Headers
subBlocks.description: Make the request headers available under "headers". Headers that carry credentials are withheld. Leave off unless you need it: exposed headers are stored in execution logs and trace spans, where they outlive the request.

subBlocks.title: Deduplication Field (Optional)
subBlocks.description: Dot-notation path to a unique field in the payload for deduplication. If the same value is seen within 7 days, the duplicate webhook will be skipped.

subBlocks.title: Acknowledgement
subBlocks.defaultValue: default

subBlocks.title: Verify Test Events
subBlocks.description: Return a temporary 200 response for test or verification probes on this webhook URL during setup.

subBlocks.title: Response Status Code
subBlocks.description: HTTP status code (100–599) to return to the webhook caller. Defaults to 200 if empty or invalid.

subBlocks.title: Response Body
subBlocks.description: JSON body to return to the webhook caller. Leave empty for no body.

subBlocks.title: Input Format
subBlocks.description: Define the expected JSON input schema for this webhook (optional). Use type "file[]" for file uploads.

subBlocks.title: Setup Instructions
subBlocks.defaultValue:
1. Copy the webhook URL and use it in your external service or API.
2. Configure your service to send webhooks to this URL.
3. The webhook accepts POST. Turn on "Accept Other HTTP Methods" to also accept GET, PUT, PATCH and DELETE — for example to trigger the workflow from a link in an email.
4. Body fields are available in your workflow, and URL query parameters under "query" (for example "query.id"). Turn on "Expose Request Headers" to also get "headers" (for example "headers.x-event-name"), and "Accept Other HTTP Methods" to also get "method".
5. Authentication is header-based, so it cannot be used with a plain link. If authentication is enabled, include the token in the Secret Header Name you configured, or in "Authorization: Bearer TOKEN" if you left it blank — only the configured one is accepted, not either.
6. To deduplicate incoming events, set the Deduplication Field to the dot-notation path of a unique identifier in the payload (e.g. "event.id"). Duplicate values within 7 days will be skipped.
7. Enable "Verify Test Events" only if the sending service needs a temporary 200 response while validating the webhook URL.

subBlocks.title: Setup Instructions
subBlocks.defaultValue:
Note: You need admin access to Gong to set up webhooks. See the Gong webhook documentation for details.
1. Copy the Webhook URL above.
2. In Gong, go to Admin center > Settings > Ecosystem > Automation rules.
3. Click "+ Add Rule" to create a new automation rule.
4. Configure rule filters in Gong for the calls you want (e.g. Call Completed). Gong does not send a separate event name in the JSON payload — filtering happens in the rule.
5. Under Actions, select "Fire webhook".
6. Paste this workflow’s Webhook URL into the destination field.
7. Authentication: Use either URL includes key (recommended default — Sim’s URL is already secret) or Signed JWT header. If you use Signed JWT, paste Gong’s public key into the field above so Sim can verify the Authorization token.
8. Save the rule and click "Save" above to activate your trigger.

granola_note_access_granted.description: Trigger workflow when a Granola note is shared with you, directly or via a folder

subBlocks.title: API Key
subBlocks.description: Your Granola API key. Used to register the webhook endpoint on deploy and remove it on undeploy.

subBlocks.title: Scopes
subBlocks.description: Comma-separated scopes deciding which notes send events: personal, public. With a Workspace API key pass exactly "workspace". Defaults to "personal, public".

subBlocks.title: Folder IDs
subBlocks.description: Optional comma-separated folder IDs (max 100). Deliveries are restricted to notes in these folders or their subfolders. Leave blank for every note matching the scopes.

subBlocks.title: Setup Instructions
subBlocks.defaultValue:
1. In the Granola desktop app, go to Settings → Connectors → API keys and click Create new key, selecting the note access scopes the key should include. See the Granola API documentation for details.
2. Paste the key into the API Key field below. Webhooks require a Granola Business or Enterprise plan.
3. Choose the Scopes that match the notes you want events for. Use workspace on its own if the key is a Workspace API key.
4. Optionally restrict deliveries to specific folders with Folder IDs.
5. Click "Save" above — Sim registers a Granola webhook endpoint for note.access_granted and verifies every delivery with the signing secret Granola returns.

event_id.description: Unique ID for the event. Retries of the same delivery reuse it.

subBlocks.placeholder: Enter the same secret key configured in Greenhouse
subBlocks.description: When set, requests must include a valid Signature header (HMAC-SHA256). If left empty, the endpoint does not verify signatures—only use on a private URL you fully control.

subBlocks.title: Setup Instructions
subBlocks.defaultValue:
1. Copy the Webhook URL above.
2. In Greenhouse, go to Configure > Dev Center > Webhooks.

7. Click Create Webhook to save.

subBlocks.title: HubSpot Account
subBlocks.description: Connect a HubSpot account so Sim can poll your CRM on your behalf.

subBlocks.description: What you want to watch.
subBlocks.defaultValue: contact

subBlocks.title: Custom Object Type ID
subBlocks.description: HubSpot custom object type ID (e.g. "2-12345"). Find it in HubSpot Settings → Objects → Custom Objects.

subBlocks.title: List
subBlocks.description: The HubSpot list to watch for new members.

subBlocks.title: Event
subBlocks.description: Created fires once per new record. Updated fires on any modification. Property Changed fires only when the chosen property changes value.
subBlocks.defaultValue: created

subBlocks.title: Property to Watch
subBlocks.description: Fires only when this specific property changes value on a record.

subBlocks.title: Properties to Fetch
subBlocks.description: Properties to include on each record. Leave empty to use sensible defaults. Sim always includes the timestamps it needs internally.

subBlocks.title: Pipeline (optional)
subBlocks.description: Restrict to a single pipeline.

subBlocks.title: Stage (optional)
subBlocks.description: Restrict to a single stage within the selected pipeline.

subBlocks.title: Owner (optional)
subBlocks.description: Restrict to records owned by a specific HubSpot user.

subBlocks.title: Advanced Filters (optional)
subBlocks.description: JSON array of HubSpot search filters, AND-combined. Each item: {"propertyName":"...","operator":"EQ","value":"..."}. Operators: EQ, NEQ, CONTAINS_TOKEN, NOT_CONTAINS_TOKEN, GT, GTE, LT, LTE, BETWEEN, IN, NOT_IN, HAS_PROPERTY, NOT_HAS_PROPERTY.

wandConfig.prompt:
You are an expert HubSpot CRM developer. Generate a JSON array of HubSpot search filters based on the user's request.

Each filter is { propertyName, operator, value }. Filters are AND-combined. The available operators are: EQ, NEQ, CONTAINS_TOKEN, NOT_CONTAINS_TOKEN, GT, GTE, LT, LTE, BETWEEN, IN, NOT_IN, HAS_PROPERTY, NOT_HAS_PROPERTY.

Dates use millisecond epoch values as strings. Strings are exact (case-sensitive) for EQ/NEQ.

User context:
{context}

Return ONLY the JSON array — no explanations, no markdown, no code fences.

subBlocks.title: Max Records Per Poll
subBlocks.description: Soft cap on records emitted per poll (default 50, max 1000). Excess rolls over to the next poll.

subBlocks.title: How it works
subBlocks.defaultValue:
1. Connect your HubSpot account above.
2. Pick the object type and event you want to watch.
3. (Optional) Restrict by pipeline, stage, owner, or advanced filters.
4. Sim polls HubSpot every minute and fires this workflow for each new or updated record.
5. The first poll establishes a baseline — only records changed after activation will fire the workflow.

objectType.description: HubSpot object type (contact, company, deal, ticket, custom object id, or list_membership)

eventType.description: Event type (created, updated, property_changed, or joined)

objectId.description: HubSpot ID of the affected record (or contact id for list memberships)

occurredAt.description: ISO timestamp of when the change happened in HubSpot

properties.description: HubSpot properties on the record as a key-value object (property internal name → value). Default keys per object type (override via "Properties to Fetch"): Contact → firstname, lastname, email, phone, company, lifecyclestage, hs_lead_status, hubspot_owner_id, createdate, lastmodifieddate. Company → name, domain, industry, lifecyclestage, hubspot_owner_id, createdate, hs_lastmodifieddate. Deal → dealname, amount, dealstage, pipeline, closedate, hubspot_owner_id, createdate, hs_lastmodifieddate. Ticket → subject, content, hs_pipeline, hs_pipeline_stage, hs_ticket_priority, hubspot_owner_id, createdate, hs_lastmodifieddate. Custom and user-requested properties appear keyed by their HubSpot internal name.

updatedAt.description: ISO timestamp when the record was last updated in HubSpot

propertyValue.description: New value of the changed property (property_changed events only)

previousValue.description: Previous value before the change (property_changed events only)

timestamp.description: ISO timestamp when Sim emitted the event

imap_poller.description: Start a workflow when an IMAP-enabled mailbox receives matching messages.

subBlocks.description: Enable SSL/TLS encryption (recommended for port 993)

subBlocks.description: Email address or username for authentication

subBlocks.title: Password
subBlocks.description: Password or app-specific password (for Gmail, use an App Password)

subBlocks.title: Mailboxes to Monitor
subBlocks.description: Choose which mailbox/folder(s) to monitor for new emails. Leave empty to monitor INBOX.

subBlocks.title: Search Criteria
subBlocks.description: ImapFlow search criteria as JSON object. Default: unseen messages only.
subBlocks.defaultValue: { "unseen": true }

wandConfig.prompt:
Generate ImapFlow search criteria as a JSON object based on the user's description.

Available properties (all are optional, combine as needed):
- "unseen": true - Unread messages
- "seen": true - Read messages
- "flagged": true - Starred/flagged messages
- "answered": true - Replied messages
- "deleted": true - Deleted messages
- "draft": true - Draft messages
- "from": "sender@example.com" - From address contains
- "to": "recipient@example.com" - To address contains
- "cc": "cc@example.com" - CC address contains
- "subject": "keyword" - Subject contains
- "body": "text" - Body contains
- "text": "search" - Headers or body contains
- "since": "2024-01-01" - Emails since date (ISO format)
- "before": "2024-12-31" - Emails before date
- "larger": 10240 - Larger than N bytes
- "smaller": 1048576 - Smaller than N bytes
- "header": { "X-Priority": "1" } - Custom header search
- "or": [{ "from": "a@x.com" }, { "from": "b@x.com" }] - OR conditions
- "not": { "from": "spam@x.com" } - Negate condition

Multiple properties are combined with AND.

Examples:
- Unread from boss: { "unseen": true, "from": "boss@company.com" }
- From Alice or Bob: { "or": [{ "from": "alice@x.com" }, { "from": "bob@x.com" }] }
- Recent with keyword: { "since": "2024-01-01", "subject": "report" }
- Exclude spam: { "unseen": true, "not": { "from": "newsletter@x.com" } }

Current criteria: {context}

Return ONLY valid JSON, no explanations or markdown.

subBlocks.title: Setup Instructions
subBlocks.defaultValue:
1. Copy the Webhook URL above.

intercom_contact_created.description: Trigger workflow when a new lead is created in Intercom

subBlocks.title: Webhook Secret
subBlocks.placeholder: Enter your Intercom app Client Secret
subBlocks.description: Your app's Client Secret from the Developer Hub. Used to verify webhook authenticity via X-Hub-Signature.

subBlocks.title: Setup Instructions
subBlocks.defaultValue:
1. Copy the Webhook URL above.
2. Go to your Intercom Developer Hub.
3. Select your app, then go to Webhooks.
4. Paste the webhook URL into the Endpoint URL field.
5. Select the contact.created topic(s).
6. Copy your app's Client Secret from the app's Basic Information page and paste it into the Webhook Secret field above (recommended for security).
7. Save the webhook configuration.
8. Deploy your workflow to activate the trigger.

jira_comment_deleted.name: Jira Comment Deleted
jira_comment_deleted.description: Trigger workflow when a comment is deleted from a Jira issue

subBlocks.title: Webhook Secret
subBlocks.description: Optional secret to validate webhook deliveries from Jira using HMAC signature

subBlocks.title: JQL Filter
subBlocks.description: Filter which comment deletions trigger this workflow using JQL

subBlocks.title: Setup Instructions
subBlocks.defaultValue:
Note: You must have admin permissions in your Jira workspace to create webhooks. See the Jira webhook documentation for details.
1. In Jira, navigate to Settings > System > WebHooks.
2. Click "Create a WebHook" to add a new webhook.
3. Paste the Webhook URL from above into the URL field.
4. Optionally, enter the Webhook Secret from above into the secret field for added security.
5. Select the events you want to trigger this workflow. For this trigger, select comment_deleted.
6. Click "Create" to activate the webhook.

jotform_webhook.name: Jotform Webhook
jotform_webhook.description: Trigger workflow when a Jotform form receives a new submission

subBlocks.title: Form ID
subBlocks.description: The form to watch. It is the numeric segment of the form URL, and the List Forms operation returns it.

subBlocks.title: API Key
subBlocks.description: Used to register the webhook on the form automatically. Create one under Account Settings > API.

subBlocks.title: Region
subBlocks.description: Data residency region the API key belongs to. A key only works on the host that issued it.

subBlocks.title: Setup Instructions
subBlocks.defaultValue:
1. Create an API key at https://www.jotform.com/myaccount/api and give it Full Access, since read-only keys cannot add webhooks
2. Pick the region your account is on. EU and HIPAA accounts are served by different hosts, and a key is rejected by every host but its own
3. Copy the Form ID from the form URL, e.g. https://www.jotform.com/build/231504059977966 gives 231504059977966
4. Sim registers the webhook on that form when you deploy the workflow, and removes it again when you undeploy
5. Note: Only submissions made through the form fire this trigger. Submissions created through the API do not.

formId.description: ID of the form that was submitted

formTitle.description: Title of the form at the time of submission

username.description: Jotform account username that owns the form

ip.description: IP address the submission came from

submissionType.description: How the submission was made, e.g. WEB

pretty.description: Human-readable summary of the answers, as comma-separated "Question Label:Answer" pairs. Unanswered questions are left out.

rawRequest.description: The submitted form body. Answers are keyed q{questionId}_{slugifiedLabel} and hold a string, or an object for a multi-part question such as name or address. A file answer instead appears under the plain slugified label as an array of upload URLs, with the chosen filenames under temp_upload. The body also carries form-internal fields such as slug, buildDate, submitSource, and jsExecutionTracker.

raw.description: Complete original webhook payload from Jotform

subBlocks.description: Validates that webhook deliveries originate from Linear.

subBlocks.title: Setup Instructions
subBlocks.defaultValue:
Note: You must have admin permissions in your Linear workspace to create webhooks.
1. In Linear, navigate to Settings > API (or Settings > Administration > API).
2. Scroll down to the Webhooks section and click "Create webhook".
3. Paste the Webhook URL from above into the URL field.
4. Optionally, enter the Webhook Secret from above into the secret field for added security.
5. Select the resource types this webhook should listen to. For this trigger, select Comment (create).
6. Click "Create" to activate the webhook.

subBlocks.title: Signing Secret

subBlocks.title: Setup Instructions
subBlocks.defaultValue:

2. In Loops, go to Settings > Webhooks and click "Add endpoint".

microsoftteams_chat_subscription.name: Microsoft Teams Chat
microsoftteams_chat_subscription.description: Trigger workflows from Microsoft Teams chat message notifications via Microsoft Graph subscriptions. Notifications share a seven-day deduplication window keyed by subscription and message ID, so later edits may not start a separate run.

subBlocks.title: Credentials
subBlocks.description: This trigger requires microsoft teams credentials to access your account.

subBlocks.title: Chat ID
subBlocks.description: The ID of the Teams chat to monitor

subBlocks.title: Include Attachments
subBlocks.description: Fetch hosted contents and upload to storage

subBlocks.title: Setup Instructions
subBlocks.defaultValue:
1. Connect your Microsoft Teams account and grant the required permissions.
2. Enter the Chat ID of the Teams chat you want to monitor.
3. We will create a Microsoft Graph change notification subscription that delivers chat message events to your Sim webhook URL.

microsoftteams_webhook.name: Microsoft Teams Channel
microsoftteams_webhook.description: Trigger workflows when the outgoing webhook is @mentioned in a Microsoft Teams channel.

subBlocks.title: HMAC Secret
subBlocks.description: The security token provided by Teams when creating an outgoing webhook. Used to verify request authenticity.

subBlocks.title: Setup Instructions
subBlocks.defaultValue:
1. Open Microsoft Teams and go to the team where you want to add the webhook. See the Microsoft Teams documentation for detailed steps.
2. Click the three dots (•••) next to the team name and select "Manage team".
3. Go to the "Apps" tab and click "Create an outgoing webhook".
4. Provide a name, description, and optionally a profile picture.
5. Set the callback URL to your Sim webhook URL above.
6. Copy the HMAC security token and paste it into the "HMAC Secret" field.
7. Click "Create" to finish setup.

notion_comment_created.name: Notion Comment Created
notion_comment_created.description: Trigger workflow when a comment or suggested edit is added in Notion

subBlocks.title: Webhook Secret
subBlocks.description: The verification_token sent by Notion during webhook setup. This same token is used to verify X-Notion-Signature HMAC headers on all subsequent webhook deliveries.

subBlocks.title: Setup Instructions
subBlocks.defaultValue:
1. Go to notion.so/profile/integrations and select your integration (or create one).
2. Navigate to the Webhooks tab.
3. Click "Create a subscription".
4. Paste the Webhook URL above into the URL field.
5. Select the comment.created event type(s).
6. Notion will send a verification request. Copy the verification_token from the payload and paste it into the Notion UI to complete verification.
7. Paste the same verification_token into the Webhook Secret field above to enable signature verification on incoming events.
8. Enable the comment read capability in your Notion integration settings so comment events can be delivered.
9. Ensure the integration has access to the pages/databases you want to monitor (share them with the integration).

entity_type.description: Entity type (comment)

subBlocks.title: Automatic Registration
subBlocks.description: Requires the Plane v2 webhook API. Use manual setup for Community Edition.

subBlocks.title: Project ID
subBlocks.description: Self-hosted v1 deletions without project information are skipped when this filter is set.

subBlocks.title: Setup Instructions
subBlocks.defaultValue:
1. Manual setup works with Plane Cloud and self-hosted Community or Commercial editions. In Plane, open Workspace settings → Webhooks and add a webhook with the URL above.
2. Select the event shown in this trigger. For v1, select the corresponding resource category. For All Events, select every category you want to receive.
3. Copy Plane’s generated secret (from the downloaded CSV or webhook edit form) into Webhook Secret below, then save the Sim configuration. Keep this secret distinct from your API token.
4. Automatic registration requires the Plane v2 webhook management API and an administrator token with webhook write permission. It creates and removes a dedicated v2 webhook when you save or remove the trigger.
5. Project filters require project information. Self-hosted v1 deletion payloads that contain only a resource ID are skipped when a project filter is set.
6. The Webhook URL must be publicly reachable from Plane. Plane v2 retries use the event ID for deduplication; v1 deliveries use a payload fingerprint.

entity_type.description: v2 entity type; null for v1.

subBlocks.title: Setup Instructions
subBlocks.defaultValue:
1. Manual setup works with Plane Cloud and self-hosted Community or Commercial editions. In Plane, open Workspace settings → Webhooks and add a webhook with the URL above.
2. Select the event shown in this trigger. For v1, select the corresponding resource category. For All Events, select every category you want to receive.
3. Copy Plane’s generated secret (from the downloaded CSV or webhook edit form) into Webhook Secret below, then save the Sim configuration. Keep this secret distinct from your API token.

6. The Webhook URL must be publicly reachable from Plane. Plane v2 retries use the event ID for deduplication; v1 deliveries use a payload fingerprint.

revenuecat_cancellation.name: RevenueCat Cancellation
revenuecat_cancellation.description: Trigger workflow when a subscriber cancels a RevenueCat subscription

subBlocks.title: API Key
subBlocks.description: Secret API key with the project_configuration:integrations:read_write permission. Sim uses it to create and remove the webhook in RevenueCat.

subBlocks.title: Project ID
subBlocks.description: RevenueCat project identifier the webhook integration is created in.

subBlocks.title: Environment
subBlocks.description: Restrict events to a single environment, or receive all of them.

subBlocks.title: Setup Instructions
subBlocks.defaultValue:
1. In the RevenueCat dashboard, go to Project settings > API keys and create a v2 Secret API key with the project_configuration:integrations:read_write permission.
2. Paste the Secret API key into the API Key field below.
3. Enter your Project ID (the proj... identifier shown in your project settings or the dashboard URL) in the Project ID field below.
4. Optionally restrict the trigger to a single Environment (Production or Sandbox). Leave it on All to receive both.
5. Sim creates the webhook integration in RevenueCat automatically when you deploy and removes it when you undeploy. This trigger fires on Cancellation events.
6. Sim generates the Authorization header secret for you and verifies every incoming request against it — you do not need to set it manually.
7. Click "Save" above to deploy and activate your trigger.

event_timestamp_ms.description: Timestamp (ms since epoch) when the event was generated

original_app_user_id.description: First App User ID ever used

aliases.description: All App User IDs ever used by the subscriber

new_product_id.description: Product identifier changed to (PRODUCT_CHANGE events only)

period_type.description: Period type (TRIAL, INTRO, NORMAL, PROMOTIONAL, or PREPAID)

presented_offering_id.description: Identifier of the offering presented to the user

is_family_share.description: Whether the purchase was family shared

country_code.description: ISO country code of the subscriber

price_in_purchased_currency.description: Price in the currency the purchase was made in

store.description: Store the purchase was made on (e.g., APP_STORE)

takehome_percentage.description: Estimated percentage of the price taken home after store commission

commission_percentage.description: Estimated percentage taken by the store as commission

offer_code.description: Offer code applied to the purchase, if any

subscriber_attributes.description: Subscriber attributes at the time of the event

experiments.description: Experiments the subscriber was enrolled in

event.description: Full RevenueCat event object

salesforce_case_status_changed.name: Salesforce Case Status Changed
salesforce_case_status_changed.description: Trigger workflow when a case status changes

subBlocks.title: Webhook Secret
subBlocks.placeholder: Generate a secret and paste it here
subBlocks.description: Required. Use the same value in your Salesforce HTTP Callout as Bearer token or X-Sim-Webhook-Secret.

subBlocks.title: Setup Instructions
subBlocks.defaultValue:
1. Copy the Webhook URL above and set a Webhook Secret. In Salesforce, create an External Credential (holding the secret) and a Named Credential whose URL is this Webhook URL, with a custom header sending the same value as Authorization: Bearer … or X-Sim-Webhook-Secret: …. If the header value uses a {!$Credential…} formula, check Allow Formulas in HTTP Header when adding it — otherwise Salesforce sends the literal formula text instead of the secret. Flow’s HTTP Callout action requires a Named Credential — it cannot call an arbitrary URL directly.
2. Under the External Credential, add a Permission Set with External Credential Principal Access enabled and assign it to the user the Flow runs as (the Automated Process user for record-triggered flows) — otherwise the callout fails authentication.
3. Go to Setup → Flows and click New Flow.
4. Select Record-Triggered Flow for the right object and Case Status Changed as the entry condition.
5. Add an HTTP Callout using the Named Credential from step 1 — POST, JSON body, path /. Record-triggered flows can only make callouts on the Run Asynchronously path, so place this action there.
6. Include eventType in the JSON body using a value this trigger accepts (e.g. for Record Created use record_created, created, or after_insert).
7. If you use Object Type (Optional), you must also include matching type metadata in the JSON body (for example objectType, sobjectType, or attributes.type) or the event will be rejected.
8. Save and Activate the Flow.
9. Click "Save" above to activate your trigger.

objectType.description: Salesforce object type (Case)

timestamp.description: When the event occurred (ISO 8601)

salesforce_webhook.name: Salesforce Webhook (All Events)
salesforce_webhook.description: Trigger workflow on any Salesforce webhook event

subBlocks.title: Webhook Secret
subBlocks.placeholder: Generate a secret and paste it here
subBlocks.description: Required. Use the same value in your Salesforce HTTP Callout as Bearer token or X-Sim-Webhook-Secret.

subBlocks.title: Object Type (Optional)
subBlocks.description: When set, the payload must include matching object type metadata (for example objectType, sobjectType, or attributes.type) or the event is rejected.

subBlocks.title: Setup Instructions
subBlocks.defaultValue:
1. Copy the Webhook URL above and generate a Webhook Secret (any strong random string). Paste the secret in the Webhook Secret field here.
2. In Salesforce, go to Setup → Named Credentials. Create an External Credential with a custom Authentication Parameter holding your secret, then a Named Credential whose URL is the Webhook URL above, with a custom header Authorization set to {!'Bearer ' & $Credential.YourExternalCredential.YourParameter} (or a header named X-Sim-Webhook-Secret with the raw secret). When adding that custom header, check Allow Formulas in HTTP Header — if left unchecked, Salesforce sends the literal {!$Credential…} text instead of evaluating it, and authentication silently fails. Flow’s HTTP Callout action requires a Named Credential — it cannot call an arbitrary URL directly.
3. Under the External Credential, add a Permission Set and enable External Credential Principal Access for its principal, then assign that permission set to the user the Flow runs as (the Automated Process user for background/record-triggered flows). Without this the callout fails authentication even though the Named Credential is configured correctly.
4. Go to Setup → Flows and click New Flow.
5. Select Record-Triggered Flow and choose the object(s) you want to monitor.
6. Add an Action that performs an HTTP Callout using the Named Credential from step 2 — method POST, Content-Type: application/json, path / (the base URL already points at your webhook). Record-triggered flows can only make callouts on the Run Asynchronously path, so place this action there.
7. Build the request body as JSON (not SOAP/XML). Include eventType and record fields (e.g. Id, Name). Outbound Messages use SOAP and will not work with this trigger.
8. Save and Activate the Flow(s).
9. Save this trigger in Sim first so the URL is registered before you build the Named Credential and Flow.
10. Click "Save" above to activate your trigger.

subBlocks.title: Webhook Secret
subBlocks.placeholder: Generate a secret and paste it here
subBlocks.description: Required. Use the same value in your ServiceNow Business Rule as Bearer token or X-Sim-Webhook-Secret.

subBlocks.title: Table Name (Optional)
subBlocks.description: Optionally filter to a specific ServiceNow table

subBlocks.title: Setup Instructions
subBlocks.defaultValue:
Note: You need admin or developer permissions in your ServiceNow instance to create Business Rules.
1. Navigate to System Definition > Business Rules and create a new Business Rule.
2. Set the table (e.g., incident, change_request), set When to after, and check Insert (record creation).
3. Check the Advanced checkbox to enable the script editor.
4. Copy the Webhook URL above and generate a Webhook Secret (any strong random string). Paste the secret in the Webhook Secret field here.
5. In the script, use RESTMessageV2 to POST the record data as JSON to the Webhook URL above. Include the secret as Authorization: Bearer <your secret> or X-Sim-Webhook-Secret: <your secret>. Example:
var r = new sn_ws.RESTMessageV2(); r.setEndpoint("<webhook_url>"); r.setHttpMethod("POST"); r.setRequestHeader("Content-Type", "application/json"); r.setRequestHeader("Authorization", "Bearer <your_webhook_secret>"); r.setRequestBody(JSON.stringify({ sysId: current.sys_id.toString(), number: current.number.toString(), shortDescription: current.short_description.toString(), state: current.state.toString(), priority: current.priority.toString() })); r.execute();
6. Activate the Business Rule and click "Save" above to activate your trigger.

subBlocks.title: TwiML Response
subBlocks.description: TwiML instructions to return immediately to Twilio. Use square brackets instead of angle brackets (e.g., [Response] instead of <Response>). This controls what happens when the call comes in (e.g., play a message, record, gather input). Your workflow will execute in the background.

wandConfig.prompt:
Generate TwiML (Twilio Markup Language) for voice calls based on the user's description.

### IMPORTANT: Use SQUARE BRACKETS instead of angle brackets
- Use [Tag] instead of <Tag>
- Use [/Tag] instead of </Tag>
- Use [Tag/] for self-closing tags instead of <Tag/>

### COMMON TWIML VERBS

**[Say]** - Text-to-speech
[Say voice="alice"]Hello, how can I help you?[/Say]
- Voices: alice, man, woman, Polly.Joanna, Polly.Matthew, etc.

**[Play]** - Play audio file
[Play]https://example.com/audio.mp3[/Play]

**[Record]** - Record caller's voice
[Record maxLength="120" transcribe="true"/]
- transcribe="true" to get text transcription

**[Gather]** - Collect keypad input or speech
[Gather input="dtmf speech" timeout="5" numDigits="1"]
  [Say]Press 1 for sales, 2 for support.[/Say]
[/Gather]

**[Dial]** - Connect to another number
[Dial]+14155551234[/Dial]

**[Pause]** - Add silence
[Pause length="2"/]

**[Hangup]** - End the call
[Hangup/]

**[Redirect]** - Redirect to another URL
[Redirect]https://example.com/next[/Redirect]

### EXAMPLES

"say hello and ask them to leave a message"
-> [Response][Say voice="alice"]Hello! Please leave a message after the beep.[/Say][Record maxLength="120" transcribe="true"/][/Response]

"greet and offer options: press 1 for sales, 2 for support"
-> [Response][Gather input="dtmf" timeout="5" numDigits="1"][Say voice="alice"]Welcome! Press 1 for sales, or press 2 for support.[/Say][/Gather][Say]Sorry, I didn't get that. Goodbye.[/Say][/Response]

"play hold music"
-> [Response][Say voice="alice"]Please hold while we connect you.[/Say][Play loop="0"]https://api.twilio.com/cowbell.mp3[/Play][/Response]

"just say please wait"
-> [Response][Say voice="alice"]Please wait while we process your request.[/Say][/Response]

"record a voicemail with transcription"
-> [Response][Say voice="alice"]You've reached our voicemail. Please leave a message.[/Say][Record transcribe="true" maxLength="180" playBeep="true"/][Say voice="alice"]Thank you for your message. Goodbye.[/Say][/Response]

Return ONLY the TwiML with square brackets - no explanations, no markdown, no extra text.
wandConfig.placeholder: Describe what should happen when a call comes in...

subBlocks.title: Setup Instructions
subBlocks.defaultValue:
1. Enter a TwiML Response above - this tells Twilio what to do when a call comes in (e.g., play a message, record, gather input). Note: Use square brackets [Tag] instead of angle brackets for TwiML tags.
2. Example TwiML for recording with transcription: [Response][Say]Please leave a message.[/Say][Record transcribe="true" maxLength="120"/][/Response]
3. Go to your Twilio Console Phone Numbers page.
4. Select the phone number you want to use for incoming calls.
5. Scroll down to the "Voice Configuration" section.
6. In the "A CALL COMES IN" field, select "Webhook" and paste the Webhook URL (from above).
7. Ensure the HTTP method is set to POST.
8. How it works: When a call comes in, Twilio receives your TwiML response immediately and executes those instructions. Your workflow runs in the background with access to caller information, call status, and any recorded/transcribed data.

whatsapp_webhook.name: WhatsApp Webhook
whatsapp_webhook.description: Trigger workflow from WhatsApp incoming messages and message status webhooks

subBlocks.title: Verification Token
subBlocks.placeholder: Generate or enter a verification token
subBlocks.description: Enter any secure token here. You'll need to provide the same token in your WhatsApp Business Platform dashboard.

subBlocks.title: App Secret
subBlocks.description: Required for WhatsApp POST signature verification. Sim uses it to validate the X-Hub-Signature-256 header on every webhook delivery.

subBlocks.title: Setup Instructions
subBlocks.defaultValue:
1. Go to your Meta App Dashboard and open the app connected to your WhatsApp Business Platform setup. If you used the WhatsApp use case flow, the configuration page may be under Use cases > Customize > Configuration instead of WhatsApp > Configuration.
2. If you do not already have an app, create one first and add the WhatsApp product before configuring webhooks.
3. Click "Save Configuration" above before verifying the callback URL so Sim has an active WhatsApp webhook config for this path. If this workflow is already deployed and you change the verification token or app secret, redeploy before re-verifying in Meta.
4. In WhatsApp > Configuration, find the Webhooks section and click Edit.
5. Paste the Webhook URL above into the "Callback URL" field.
6. Paste the Verification Token into the "Verify token" field.
7. Copy your app's App Secret from App Settings > Basic and paste it into the App Secret field above so Sim can validate POST signatures.
8. Click "Verify and save".
9. Click Manage next to webhook fields and subscribe to messages. That field covers incoming messages and outbound message status updates.

eventType.description: Webhook classification such as incoming_message, message_status, or mixed

messageId.description: First WhatsApp message identifier (wamid) found in the webhook batch

from.description: Sender phone number from the first incoming message in the batch

recipientId.description: Recipient phone number from the first status update in the batch

phoneNumberId.description: Business phone number ID from the first message or status item in the batch

displayPhoneNumber.description: Business display phone number from the first message or status item in the batch

text.description: Text body from the first incoming text message in the batch

timestamp.description: Timestamp from the first message or status item in the batch

messageType.description: Type of the first incoming message in the batch (text, image, system, etc.)

mediaId.description: Media asset ID from the first incoming media message. Pass to the Download Media operation to fetch the file. Expires after 7 days.

mediaMimeType.description: MIME type of the first incoming media message

caption.description: Caption on the first incoming image, video, or document message

status.description: First outgoing message status in the batch, such as sent, delivered, read, or failed

contact.description: First sender contact in the batch (wa_id, profile.name)

webhookContacts.description: All sender contact profiles from the webhook batch

messages.description: All incoming message objects from the webhook batch, flattened across entries/changes

statuses.description: All message status objects from the webhook batch, flattened across entries/changes

conversation.description: Conversation metadata from the first status update in the batch (id, expiration_timestamp, origin.type)

pricing.description: Pricing metadata from the first status update in the batch (billable, pricing_model, category)

raw.description: Complete structured webhook payload from WhatsApp

zoho_desk.name: Zoho Desk Event
zoho_desk.description: Trigger a workflow when a Zoho Desk event occurs (ticket, comment, thread, contact, agent, task, or article changes).

subBlocks.title: Zoho Desk Account
subBlocks.description: This trigger creates and manages a webhook subscription in your Zoho Desk account.

subBlocks.title: Organization
subBlocks.description: The Zoho Desk organization (portal) to subscribe in.

subBlocks.title: Organization ID
subBlocks.description: Type an organization ID instead of picking one from the list.

subBlocks.title: Department IDs (optional)
subBlocks.description: Restrict events to these departments. Leave empty for all departments.

subBlocks.title: Watched Fields (optional)
subBlocks.placeholder: Up to 5 comma-separated field API names
subBlocks.description: For Ticket Updated: only fire when one of these fields changes (max 5). Previous values are included in the payload.

subBlocks.title: Setup Instructions
subBlocks.defaultValue:
1. Connect your Zoho Desk account above with OAuth — the trigger provisions its webhook through an OAuth connection and cannot use a Self Client. Webhooks require a Zoho Desk edition of Professional or higher (Free and Standard cannot create webhooks). The OAuth connection supports accounts in the US data center (accounts.zoho.com) only, so organizations in other regions cannot use this trigger yet.
2. Select your Organization from the dropdown (populated automatically from your connected Zoho Desk account).
3. Choose the event to subscribe to. For "Ticket Updated" you can optionally list up to 5 ticket field API names to watch; previous field values are included in the payload. For "Ticket Thread Added" you can filter by direction (incoming/outgoing).
4. Optionally restrict events to specific departments by entering comma-separated department IDs.
5. Click Save above. Sim creates the webhook subscription in Zoho Desk for you and tears it down automatically when the workflow is undeployed.

eventType.description: The Zoho Desk event type (e.g. Ticket_Add)

eventTime.description: Event time in milliseconds since epoch

payload.description: The full resource that changed (ticket, comment, thread, etc.). Comment and thread events gain a derived plain-text `contentText` alongside the raw `content` + `contentType`; ticket events gain `descriptionText` alongside `description`.

prevState.description: Previous state of the resource (update events only)

zoom_meeting_ended.name: Zoom Meeting Ended
zoom_meeting_ended.description: Trigger workflow when a Zoom meeting ends

subBlocks.title: Secret Token
subBlocks.placeholder: Enter your Zoom app Secret Token
subBlocks.description: Found in your Zoom app's Features page. Required for endpoint validation and webhook signature verification.

subBlocks.title: Setup Instructions
subBlocks.defaultValue:
1. Copy the Webhook URL above.
2. Go to the Zoom Marketplace and create or open a Webhook-only or general app with Event Subscriptions enabled (Meeting / Recording events as needed). Admin approval may be required for account-level webhooks.
3. Copy the Secret Token from your Zoom app's Features page and paste it in the Secret Token field above.
4. Click "Save Configuration" above to activate the trigger.
5. Navigate to Features > Event Subscriptions and click Add Event Subscription.
6. Enter a subscription name and paste the webhook URL into the Event notification endpoint URL field.
7. Click Validate to verify the endpoint.
8. Click Add Events and select the meeting.ended event type.
9. Save the event subscription in Zoom.

event_ts.description: Unix timestamp in milliseconds when the event occurred

object.description: Meeting details (shape aligns with Zoom Meetings webhook object fields)

meeting_type.description: Meeting type (1=instant, 2=scheduled, etc.; maps to Zoom `type`)

host_email.description: Host email address (when provided by Zoom)

end_time.description: Meeting end time (ISO 8601, present on meeting.ended)

join_url.description: URL for participants to join (when provided)

status.description: Meeting status (e.g. waiting, started; when provided)

created_at.description: Creation timestamp in ISO 8601 format (when provided)
